2.text: put on the heavy fur shirts of the Chukchee when they drive a reindeer-sledge.

3.text: Their own clothing does not sufficiently protect them from the heavy wind

4.text: blowing against their faces, and from the lumps of snow thrown up by the

5.text: reindeer-hoofs and the runners of the sledges.

6.text: Each part of the Chukchee winter garments for men or women is made

7.text: in two pieces, an inner and an outer one, the former with the hair side in,

8.text: and the latter with the hair side out. These pieces are worn without being

9.text: sewed together, in order that they may be separated for drying, but they fit

10.text: together so exactly as to form practically a single garment. The inner part

11.text: is usually made of very soft-haired material, so that it will not irritate the

12.text: skin, and can be worn without underclothing even by a European.

13.text: The chief piece of clothing is a heavy fur shirt almost reaching to the

14.text: knees, with no hood attached, and with a rather large opening in the collar

15.text: (Plates XXIII, Fig. 1; XXIV, Fig. 2; also Fig. 168). Koryak shirts are longer,
15.note: Roman numerals XXIII/XXIV keyed plain ASCII caps per keying_spec.md §2.12 regardless of the printed small-cap setting. 16.text: and often have a hood; but among the Chukchee only the shroud has a hood,

17.text: which is drawn over the face of the dead body. The shroud is therefore

18.text: called by them “the hooded garment.” The collar of the Chukchee shirt is
18.note: Machine draft rendered the closing quote as a straight/escaped \" ; 2x zoom (zoom2-18p30-98_24p9-82.png) shows a curly closing quotation mark ” after 'garment.', per §1/§5.6 (quotes are always curly, not a raster question).

19.text: bound with a narrow piece of skin folded over so that a stout sinew string

20.text: may be pulled through to tighten the collar as much as desired. The ends

21.text: of the string come out on the breast. The Chukchee assert that the string

22.text: is added to strengthen the neck of the shirt in case of a scuffle; otherwise

23.text: it would give way when pulled hard in wrestling.

24.text: The shirts of the Maritime people, (Plate XXIV, Fig. 1) are of the same cut
